\section{Experimental Setup}

\subsection{Models and Data}

We use \textbf{Pythia-410M-deduped} (405M parameters, $D{=}1024$) as the primary model and \textbf{Pythia-1B-deduped} (1042M parameters, $D{=}2048$) for scale-transfer validation.
Both are decoder-only transformers pretrained on the deduplicated Pile~\cite{gerstgrasser2024}.

From The Pile (deduplicated), we sample three disjoint subsets:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Training pool}: 50K sequences of 512 tokens for fine-tuning.
  \item \textbf{Evaluation set}: 5K held-out sequences for perplexity measurement.
  \item \textbf{Spectral probe set}: 1K held-out sequences for effective rank computation.
\end{itemize}
All tokenization uses the GPTNeoX tokenizer (vocabulary size 50{,}304).

\subsection{Recursive Training Protocol}

Generation~0 is the pretrained checkpoint with no additional fine-tuning.
For each subsequent generation $t = 1, \ldots, T$ with $T{=}10$:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item \textbf{Synthetic generation.} Sample 50K sequences from $M_{t-1}$ using nucleus-free ancestral sampling (temperature $= 1.0$, top-$k = 50$, max length 512 tokens).
  \item \textbf{Data mixing.} Combine synthetic samples with real data at condition-specific ratio $r_t$ (see \S\ref{sec:conditions}).
  \item \textbf{Fine-tuning.} Train $M_{t-1}$ for 1 epoch on the mixed corpus $\rightarrow M_t$.
  \item \textbf{Checkpoint and evaluate.} Save $M_t$; measure all metrics on held-out data.
\end{enumerate}

Training hyperparameters are fixed across all conditions: AdamW optimizer with learning rate $5{\times}10^{-5}$, weight decay $0.01$, batch size~8 with gradient accumulation~4 (effective batch size~32), linear warmup over 5\% of steps followed by linear decay, and gradient clipping at $\|\mathbf{g}\|_{\max} = 1.0$.

\subsection{Evaluation Metrics}

\paragraph{Effective Rank (RankMe).}
Following \citet{rankme2023}, we forward-pass the 1K spectral probe set through $M_t$, extract last-layer hidden states, mean-pool across sequence length to obtain $\mathbf{Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{1000 \times D}$, compute its SVD, and report $\rho(\mathbf{Z}) = \exp(H(\mathbf{p}))$ where $\mathbf{p}$ is the normalized singular value distribution.
Lower effective rank signals representation collapse.

\paragraph{Held-out Perplexity.}
Standard token-level cross-entropy loss on the 5K evaluation set, reported as $\text{PPL} = \exp(\mathcal{L})$.

\paragraph{Distinct-4.}
The ratio of unique 4-grams to total 4-grams in 1K samples generated from $M_t$ (temperature~1.0, top-$k$~50), measuring lexical diversity of generation.

\paragraph{HellaSwag Accuracy.}
Zero-shot normalized accuracy (acc\_norm) via \texttt{lm-evaluation-harness}, measuring downstream commonsense reasoning capability.

\paragraph{Expected Calibration Error (ECE).}
Token-level calibration on the held-out evaluation set with 10 equal-width bins.
Prior work shows ECE degradation precedes accuracy loss~\cite{calibration2025}; we track it as a secondary early-warning indicator alongside effective rank.

\subsection{Experimental Conditions}
\label{sec:conditions}

All non-collapse conditions share an identical total real-data budget $B = T \times r_{\text{base}} = 10 \times 0.50 = 5.0$ (in units of dataset-equivalents), ensuring differences arise solely from temporal allocation:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  \item \textbf{Pure synthetic} ($r_t = 0 \;\forall t$): collapse reference with no real-data intervention.
  \item \textbf{Fixed uniform} ($r_t = 0.50 \;\forall t$): static baseline distributing budget equally across generations.
  \item \textbf{Spectral-guided adaptive} (ours): closed-loop proportional controller (\S3.3) using effective rank as the feedback signal. Controller parameters: $\tau = 0.02$, $k = 2.0$, $\alpha = 0.5$, $r_{\min} = 0.10$, $r_{\max} = 0.90$.
  \item \textbf{Linear-increasing} ($r_t$ linearly from 0.30 to 0.70): open-loop heuristic baseline that front-loads synthetic data and back-loads real data without feedback.
\end{enumerate}

Conditions (b), (c), and (d) consume exactly the same total real data ($B = 5.0$); only the temporal distribution differs.
This iso-budget design isolates the effect of \emph{when} real data is introduced from \emph{how much} is used~\cite{garg2025, data_mixing_laws2024}.

\subsection{Statistical Design}

Each condition is run with 3 random seeds, paired across conditions (i.e., all four conditions share the same seed set) to reduce variance from initialization and data ordering.
We report mean $\pm$ standard deviation across seeds.

Significance testing uses paired $t$-tests on per-seed final metrics.
Effect sizes are reported as Cohen's $d$ with 95\% bootstrap confidence intervals (10{,}000 resamples).
We pre-register two primary hypotheses:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item Adaptive vs.\ fixed uniform: $\geq$3 perplexity point improvement at generation~$T$.
  \item Closed-loop (adaptive) vs.\ open-loop (linear-increasing): $\geq$1.5 perplexity point improvement at generation~$T$.
\end{enumerate}

Results tables follow the format: [PLACEHOLDER---final numeric results pending experiment completion].
EOF
